newsitem.title: USA: Caliber System to close units, eliminate 4,000 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Caliber System to close units, eliminate 4,000 jobs.

text.p: Calibre System Inc. said Thursday it will close its Coles Express and Spartan Express units, eliminating 4,000 jobs, and sell off its Central Freight Lines unit in a restructuring of the trucking company.
Calibre System, formerly Roadway Services, said it is negotiating with several potential buyers for the Central Freight Lines unit, which serves customers in the Southwest.
Currently, Calibre's Coles Express unit operates in the Northeast and Spartan Express operates in the Southeast and Midwest. Operations will cease immediately, the company said.

Calibre's freight operations will be consolidating into the struggling Viking Freight Inc. unit, which will continue to operate in the 12 western states with next- and second-day less-than-truckload service.
"The losses generated by Viking have been unacceptable," said Chairman Daniel Sullivan.

"The length of time needed to reach profitability in all of Viking's divisions was too long and filled with risk. We examined all of our options and determined that a major restructuring was the most viable alternative for enhancing Viking's financial stability and returning the unit to profitability.
"These actions will ensure a much stronger Calibre System and maximize value for our shareholders," Sullivan said.
Excluding Viking, the combined business units earned an operating profit in 1996 of more than $150 million.

However, Calibre System is restating its previously reported 1996 profits of $9.9 million, or 25 cents a share, to a net loss of $165.1 million, or $4.18 a share, to reflect charges and writedowns, the company said.
Additional charges will be reported in the first quarter of 1997 to include employee severance and other costs, Calibre System said.
Additionally, Calibre System said it is cutting its quarterly cash dividend to 10 cents a share, from 18 cents a share, payable Aug. 1 to holders of record July 15.
Calibre stock rose 62.5 cents to $26.625 on the New York Stock Exchange. The announcement was made after the close of trading.
